description: Canonical machine-readable registry of Identity Agent action codes. Integer `code` (t) is the canonical wire identifier; `key` is the stable human/URL handle (used as ?action= in OOBI URLs and as the share_actions.action_key). This file is the single source of truth: it seeds identity.db and is imported by any Identity Agent. See docs/action-code-registry.md for the spec + governance.

actions.name: Sign in
actions.summary: Authenticate to a relying party (website/app/device) with a pairwise identity.
actions.outcome: The agent presents a pairwise AID (per-RP by default; anchored to a chosen identity when relationship_anchor_aid is set), signs the challenge, and the RP verifies and optionally applies its access policy.

actions.name: Add Contact
actions.summary: A mutual, front-facing "we know each other" contact ceremony between two agents.
actions.outcome: Each side records the other as a contact at the chosen tier (distinct from low-level transactional KERI contacts, which are automatic and unceremonious).

actions.name: Add Employee
actions.summary: An organization invites an individual to become an employee; the individual's agent presents a stable per-org pairwise identity to be enrolled.
actions.outcome: The individual derives/reuses a stable pairwise AID for the org and is added to the counterpart's roster (pending -> active on approval). The code + schema are universal; the roster/approval mechanics are an implementation concern.

actions.name: Sign an Organization
actions.summary: An individual attests (vouches) that a real person stands behind a newly created organization, becoming its founding owner (the super-admin role).
actions.outcome: The individual signs a vouch over the organization's AID (stored by the counterpart as proof) and is enrolled as the active owner (the super-admin role). No delegated inception — the organization controls its own keys; the signer only attests.

actions.name: Sign a statement
actions.summary: A utility app asks a person to sign a statement with their own Identity Agent's root key, after reading exactly what it says, so the utility app can prove the person said it. Code 5 stays reserved as issue (ADR-021).
actions.outcome: The person's Identity Agent signs, with the root key in force, the envelope in docs/statement-signature.md (a fixed header, the asker's identifier, the statement exactly as shown) and posts the signature, the signer's identifier and the sequence number of the key event the key was set at to the asker's callback. Nothing is signed without the person's approval on that device.

actions.name: Join a site with one identity
actions.summary: An organization asks a person to say that their identifier at one of the organization's sites and an identifier they already have with the organization are the same person; the person's Identity Agent signs one statement with both keys.

preview_contract.title: Join {site} as the same person you are to {org}.

actions.outcome: The individual's Identity Agent derives its identifier for the site, signs one statement naming both identifiers, the organization, the site and the invite with the key of each, and sends it to the organization, which checks both signatures. Declining signs nothing. The linking is the point of it, so the individual is told it cannot be undone except by leaving.
